newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's HK chief heads west to explain policies.
newsitem.headline: China's HK chief heads west to explain policies.

text.p: China is despatching its Hong Kong policy chief, Lu Ping, to Europe and Canada to try to assure governments and business about the territory's future as part of China, a pro-China newspaper said on Friday.
Lu, the director of Beijing's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, would visit Germany and Austria between March 16 and 26, the Beijing-controlled daily Wen Wei Pao said.

In April he would go to other European countries and Canada, which has a big community of Hong Kong Chinese who have emigrated in recent years out of fears over Beijing's imminent control of Hong Kong.
A British colony for more than 150 years, Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
Lu would give assurances to governments and businessmen that Hong Kong would enjoy considerable self-rule after the handover.

Under a Sino-British handover treaty, Hong Kong has been promised a high degree of autonomy and the continuation of its capitalist way of life under a "one country, two systems" formula for the next 50 years.

Lu's tour is an eleventh-hour gesture by Beijing to lobby the West, after a series of tours by leading Hong Kong democrats who have warned of China's plan to cut civil rights and roll back democracy in the territory after July 1.
Chinese leaders and pro-China politicians in Hong Kong have said the Western media are giving a distorted, alarmist picture of Hong Kong's destiny when it reverts to China.
